subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-demo follow-up

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps so we keep momentum on sizing dedicated capacity to hit your SLOs. Key takeaways: 

- SLOs you mentioned: 95th percentile generation latency <= 300ms for 512-token responses (interactive chat), sustained concurrency of ~40 concurrent users, and ability to stream token-by-token for UI.
- Typical workload: mixture of short answers (~64 tokens) and occasional long-form (~512 tokens); expected steady-state throughput ~120 requests/minute with bursts to 300 RPM during peaks.
- Preferred GPU constraints: you asked about cost/latency tradeoffs between A100 and H100 class GPUs and whether newer L4/L40s variants make sense for inference.

Attached: a first-pass dedicated-sizing proposal and our internal GPU benchmark summary (pdf/xlsx). Marissa and Rafael — can you confirm the CPU/memory/network assumptions I used and call out any configs we should avoid for streaming workloads?

Next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood to run a focused perf validation for your mix: 64/512 token split, concurrency 40, streaming enabled. Deliverables: latency P95/P99, throughput by GPU type, and recommended reserved throughput sizing. (Target: results in 5 business days)
2) Acme to provide a sample traffic profile (anonymized) and a representative prompt set + a couple of long-chat transcripts to validate KV-cache behavior.
3) Align on preferred GPU family and commit window for Dedicated.

Let me know if the summary matches your notes. Happy to schedule a 30-min follow-up with Marissa to walk through the sizing doc.

Cheers,
Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-demo follow-up

Thanks Aditya — that matches our notes. A couple of clarifications: 

- The 300ms P95 target is for user-facing generations where we can't defer streaming; for background batch jobs we care more about throughput than latency.
- Concurrency: 40 concurrent *active* users on chat; each active user issues ~1.5 requests/minute on average. So steady-state concurrency is lower but peak matters for UX.
- Streaming: absolutely required for chat. We need per-token streaming with low startup latency (<= 100ms first token ideally).

We'll share an anonymized traffic sample and a few convo transcripts by EOD tomorrow.

-Sarah
VP Product | Acme AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation - post-demo follow-up

Hi Sarah / Aditya — thanks for the quick clarifications, Sarah. A few notes from the engineering side after I reviewed your profile and the benchmarks: 

Summary of validation plan I'll run:
- Workload profile: 70% short (32-128 tokens), 30% long (~512 tokens). Mix will be configurable.
- Metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency, startup latency (first-token), tokens/sec, end-to-end throughput (requests/sec), GPU util, and KV cache hit rate.
- Concurrency targets: baseline test at 40 concurrent active users, spike tests up to 120 concurrent sessions to validate graceful degradation and autoscale triggers.
- Streaming: we'll validate per-token streaming with chunk sizes matching your frontend; measure first-byte time and steady-state token delivery rate.

GPU family comparison (high level):
- H100 (fp16/amp): best single-request latency for large models and higher memory; expect ~15-30% better latency vs A100 for long-context workloads, but higher cost.
- A100: reliable for mixed workloads, good memory; slightly higher latency vs H100 on our kernels but cheaper in many clouds.
- L40s / L4: cost-effective for smaller models and heavy streaming workloads where memory is less constrained; may need model quantization for parity on accuracy.

Preliminary sizing guidance (subject to perf run):
- To achieve P95 <= 300ms for 512 tokens with streaming enabled, estimated reserved throughput: 30-50 tokens/sec per GPU for large 70B-style models (higher for H100). For smaller quantized 13B/8B models you can get 3-4x tokens/sec.
- For concurrency 40 with mixed short/long mix, start with 4-6 GPUs (H100) or 6-10 GPUs (A100), then right-size after validation.

Deliverables: detailed perf report (spreadsheet + charts), recommended reserved throughput and autoscale policy, and a suggested failover plan (fallback to cheaper model variant).

I'll kick off the validation once we have the traffic sample + prompt set. Rafael — can you help coordinate infra and the target run windows? I've attached the detailed benchmark sheet with test configs.

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks team — scheduling note: I've reserved a validation window tomorrow 09:00-13:00 PST and queued the perf jobs. Aditya: can you confirm Acme will upload the anonymized traffic sample to the shared Drive link and drop a comment with required model variants (13B quantized, 70B fp16) by EOD tonight?

Quick infra assumptions I used:
- Network: 25Gbps NIC per host; NVMe-backed local cache for KV prefix caching.
- CPU: 16 vCPU host to avoid host-side bottlenecks during high-concurrency streaming.
- Autoscale policy: start with reserved capacity for baseline, autoscale-on-queue-growth for burst to avoid cold start latency.

If all good I'll run the baseline H100 / A100 / L40s matrix and share preliminary charts by 5pm tomorrow.

-Rafael
Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
